english.title: Permit setting of a snare to injure a wild animal
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowingly permitted to be set in position a self-locking snare which was of such a nature and so placed as to be calculated to cause bodily injury to any wild animal coming into contact with it
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 11(1)(d) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) See Section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(ii) Section 21(5) provides that where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each.
(iii) See Section 27 for meaning of "wild animal".
(iv) See Section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
(v) As amended by paragraph 10 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.
(vi) See also offence wording: H4656.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each animal (Section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation
